Side effects:

Astringency: 100% DMSO usually irritates skin on the upper half of the body. When the skin itches, dilute the DMSO with water or real aloe juice without added chemicals. Leaving 100% DMSO on the skin can crenate (shrivel) it, and the skin may take a week to look plump again. DMSO can also burn dry mouth tissue, so wet your mouth first.
Nausea: when drinking DMSO, dilute it in water, juice, or milk and sip gradually. Sensitivity to DMSO varies, so start with less than you planned.
Reduced sleep: DMSO reduces how long I sleep when I take too much, take it too late, or use it over too many consecutive days. It builds up past a threshold that seems to differ between people, so it's best taken in the morning, and reduce the dose if you notice you're sleeping less. In rats, higher doses of DMSO made sleep less deep. Some people sleep better with DMSO because it reduces whatever symptom had been keeping them awake.
Body odor: above a certain dose you may smell like sulfur. I don't smell when I put it into milk.

During a trip, try not to take every dark thought that comes up as the truth about you, since it's often just the flip side of whatever you've been focusing on. Pushing the thought away tends to make it come back stronger, so let it be there. You can tell the person sitting with you, but maybe hold off on confessing it to everybody else, or deciding it means something is permanently wrong with you. Just notice what's there: "A thought is here. A feeling is here. It is intense, but it is not the whole of me." Then return to room, body, human, time, and love.
